page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on KVM virtualization. Powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It contains no bundled local storage or hardware GPUs, relying on remote block storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Cache architecture comprises 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, complemented by instruction set support including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 vector extensions.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core (1993.0) and stress-ng single-core (3071.48) workloads, alongside strong text processing scores (2509.0). Multi-core throughput remains in the average tier, with a 4533.0 Geekbench multi-core score and 7541.77 in PassMark CPU tests. The memory subsystem demonstrates average performance on write operations (27.98 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks) but registers lower-tier throughput on uncached reads (37.76 GB/sec) and PassMark database operations, accompanied by 5.72 million Redis SET operations per second.

The absence of integrated local storage and a moderate 2 Gbps baseline network interface require architectural consideration for high-throughput I/O setups. However, the high RAM allocation relative to core count delivers solid resource efficiency for memory-heavy tasks that do not demand extensive thread parallelization. Suitable workloads include in-memory caching systems, enterprise application backends, staging database environments, and memory-constrained data transformation pipelines.

Driven by KVM, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core), and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local disks and no GPU accelerators. Its CPU architecture includes AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-thread compute in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, alongside average multi-core processing power and moderate memory bandwidth. The generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers efficient resource density for memory-bound applications with modest concurrency needs, making it well matched for in-memory caches, middleware services, staging database instances, and general memory-intensive background processing.
